newsitem.title: USA: Suit seeks to block DeKalb County, Ga., tax vote.
newsitem.headline: Suit seeks to block DeKalb County, Ga., tax vote.

text.p: Three residents of Georgia's DeKalb County have filed suit seeking to block the county's March 18 referendum on a proposal to raise sales taxes to build schools, Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported Friday.
The suit contends that the DeKalb County School Board incorrectly calculated how the tax revenue would be divided among the three school systems in the county, City of Atlanta and City of Decatur.

The proposal would increase the sales tax by one cent, raising $532 million over five years. The plaintiffs said Atlanta schools would be shortchanged by $1.5 million and Decatur schools would be shortchanged by about $1 million under the proposed revenue distribution plan.
DeKalb County School Superintendnet J. Reynolds Hallford said he had not yet seen the lawsuit but that "We believe we have followed the dictates of the legislation as it has been directed to us."

The school sales tax is one of two proposed sales tax increases on the countywide ballot March 18. The other would raise the tax by an additional cent to offset a 40 pecent rollback in property taxes.
If both are approved, the sales tax would rise to 7 percent from 5 percent.
